1.summary: Paul thanks God for the Thessalonians' work of faith, labor of love and steadfast hope, recalling how the gospel came with power and how they turned from idols to serve the living God and wait for his Son, becoming an example across Greece.
1.lookfor: Notice the trio of faith, love and hope, and the three-part description of conversion at the end.

names.name: Silvanus
names.gloss: Silas, Paul's travel companion on the second journey.

names.name: Timothy
names.gloss: Paul's young co-worker, who had just visited them.

names.name: Thessalonians
names.gloss: Believers in Thessalonica, capital of Macedonia.

insights.title: Faith, love, hope
insights.body: Paul remembers their work of faith, labor of love and patience of hope (1:3). Each virtue is active: faith works, love toils, hope endures.

insights.title: Not in word only
insights.body: The gospel came not only in word but in power, in the Holy Spirit and with much assurance (1:5). Paul points to what they saw and experienced, not just what they heard.

insights.title: Much affliction
insights.body: They received the word in much affliction, with joy of the Holy Spirit (1:6). Acts tells of a mob attacking Jason's house and forcing Paul to leave by night.

insights.title: An example
insights.body: They became an example to all the believers in Macedonia and Achaia; the word sounded out from them so Paul didn't need to say anything (1:7-8). Thessalonica stood on the main Roman road, the Via Egnatia, so news travelled fast.

insights.title: Turned, serve, wait
insights.body: They turned to God from idols, to serve the living and true God, and to wait for his Son from heaven (1:9-10). A complete summary of conversion: a turn, a new service, a new hope.

insights.title: Rescued from wrath
insights.body: Jesus delivers us from the wrath to come (1:10). The coming judgment is real, but believers wait in hope, not dread.

insights.title: What echoes
insights.body: The Thessalonians' faith became known far beyond their city. What story does your faith tell to the people who watch you?

2.summary: Paul defends his conduct in Thessalonica: he came boldly despite mistreatment in Philippi, didn't flatter or seek money or glory, was gentle as a nursing mother and encouraging as a father, and thanks God that they received the message as God's word, even under persecution from their own countrymen.
2.lookfor: Notice the mother and father images, and why Paul worked night and day.

names.name: Philippi
names.gloss: Where Paul and Silas had been beaten and jailed just before.

names.name: Judea
names.gloss: The region around Jerusalem, where the first churches also suffered.

names.name: Satan
names.gloss: The adversary, who hindered Paul's return.

insights.title: Wandering teachers
insights.body: Philosophers and religious teachers roamed Greek cities seeking followers and fees, often with flattery. Paul distances himself: no flattery, no greed, no seeking glory (2:5-6).

insights.title: Like a nursing mother
insights.body: We were gentle among you, like a nursing mother cherishing her own children (2:7). Paul shared not only the gospel but his own life (2:8).

insights.title: Working night and day
insights.body: Paul worked night and day so as not to burden anyone (2:9). He supported himself as a tentmaker so no one could accuse him of preaching for money.

insights.title: Like a father
insights.body: As a father with his children, we exhorted, comforted and urged each one of you to walk worthy of God (2:11-12). Mother and father together: tender care and firm guidance.

insights.title: The word of God
insights.body: You received it not as the word of men, but as it truly is, the word of God, which works in you who believe (2:13). The message carries its own power.

insights.title: Our glory and joy
insights.body: You are our glory and our joy (2:20). Paul's crown at Christ's coming will be people, not achievements.

insights.title: Sharing your life
insights.body: Paul shared not only the message but his very self. Whom are you investing your life in, not just your words?

3.summary: Unable to bear the separation, Paul sent Timothy from Athens to strengthen them; Timothy returned with good news of their faith and love, which revived Paul, and he prays to see them again and for their love to increase.
3.lookfor: Notice how Paul's emotions rise and fall with news of them, and his prayer at the end.

names.name: Athens
names.gloss: Where Paul waited alone while Timothy went to Thessalonica.

names.name: Timothy
names.gloss: Paul's brother and God's fellow worker.

insights.title: Left alone in Athens
insights.body: Paul was willing to be left alone in Athens (3:1) to send Timothy. Acts tells of Paul debating there while waiting for his companions.

insights.title: Appointed to affliction
insights.body: Paul had told them in advance that we are appointed to suffer affliction (3:3-4). Persecution didn't mean the gospel had failed.

insights.title: Now we live
insights.body: Now we live, if you stand fast in the Lord (3:8). Timothy's report brought Paul back to life; his wellbeing was bound up with theirs.

insights.title: What is lacking
insights.body: Paul prays night and day to see them and supply what is lacking in their faith (3:10). The word is used of mending nets, filling gaps left by his hurried departure.

insights.title: Increase and abound in love
insights.body: May the Lord make you increase and abound in love for one another and for all (3:12). Love for all, not just fellow believers, echoes Jesus' command to love even enemies.

insights.title: Blameless at his coming
insights.body: Paul prays they will be blameless in holiness before God at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all his saints (3:13). The return of Christ is woven through every chapter.

insights.title: Good news of others
insights.body: Paul was revived by hearing that others were standing firm. Whose faith could you encourage by letting them know how they've encouraged you?

4.summary: Paul urges sexual purity and brotherly love, quiet lives and honest work, then comforts them about believers who have died: they will rise first when the Lord descends, and together all will meet him and be with him forever.
4.lookfor: Notice the reason Paul gives for not grieving as others do, and the vivid picture of the Lord's coming.

insights.title: Purity in a permissive world
insights.body: Paul calls them to abstain from sexual immorality and control their bodies in holiness, not in lustful passion like the Gentiles (4:3-5). Greek and Roman society tolerated much that the gospel forbade.

insights.title: Mind your own business
insights.body: Aspire to live quietly, mind your own affairs, and work with your hands (4:11), so outsiders respect you and you depend on no one. Some may have stopped working while waiting for Jesus.

insights.title: Grief with hope
insights.body: Paul doesn't want them to grieve like others who have no hope (4:13). Ancient epitaphs often expressed hopelessness; one reads, I was not, I was, I am not, I care not. Christians grieve, but with hope.

insights.title: Fallen asleep
insights.body: Paul speaks of believers who have fallen asleep (4:13-15), a gentle picture of death as temporary rest before waking. The word cemetery comes from the Greek for sleeping place.

insights.title: Meeting the Lord
insights.body: We will be caught up to meet the Lord in the air (4:17). The word for meeting was used when citizens went out to welcome a visiting emperor and escort him back into their city.

insights.title: Forever with the Lord
insights.body: With a shout, the archangel's voice and God's trumpet, the dead in Christ will rise first; so we will always be with the Lord (4:16-17). The heart of the hope is being with him.

insights.title: Comfort one another
insights.body: Paul says to comfort one another with these words (4:18). Who do you know who is grieving and needs this hope?

5.summary: The day of the Lord will come like a thief, but believers are children of light and should stay awake, armed with faith, love and hope; Paul closes with a stream of short commands for church life and a prayer that God will sanctify them completely.
5.lookfor: Notice the night and day imagery, and the rapid commands in verses 12 to 22.

insights.title: Like a thief
insights.body: The day of the Lord comes like a thief in the night (5:2), as Jesus taught. The day of the Lord was the prophets' term for God's decisive judgment and rescue.

insights.title: Peace and safety
insights.body: When people say peace and safety, sudden destruction comes (5:3). Peace and security was a Roman slogan, stamped on coins and proclaimed as the empire's gift.

insights.title: Children of the day
insights.body: You are all children of light and of the day (5:5). The day hasn't fully come, but believers belong to it already, so they stay awake and sober.

insights.title: Armor again
insights.body: Put on the breastplate of faith and love, and for a helmet, the hope of salvation (5:8), echoing Isaiah's picture of God's armor, developed later in Ephesians.

insights.title: Rejoice, pray, give thanks
insights.body: Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, in everything give thanks, for this is God's will for you (5:16-18). Short commands that shape a whole way of life.

insights.title: Spirit, soul and body
insights.body: May God sanctify you completely, spirit, soul and body (5:23). Paul isn't giving a technical map of human nature, just saying all of you.

insights.title: He will do it
insights.body: He who calls you is faithful, who will also do it (5:24). Holiness is God's work in us before it is our effort.

insights.title: In everything
insights.body: Paul says to give thanks in everything, not for everything. What could you thank God for in the middle of a hard situation?

intro.who: Paul, Silvanus (Silas) and Timothy (1:1), to the church in Thessalonica, founded on Paul's second journey before he was forced to leave (Acts 17:1-10).
intro.when: About AD 50–51, from Corinth, a few months after Paul left. It may be his earliest surviving letter and among the oldest writings in the New Testament.
intro.why: Timothy brought good news of the young church's faith under persecution (3:6). Paul writes to encourage them, defend his conduct against slander, urge holy living, and answer their grief over believers who had died before Jesus' return.

outline.title: Thanksgiving and Paul's love for them
Holy living and the hope of the dead
The day of the Lord and life together
